activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 7 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: Implementing a plan means discussing it without taking action.
cards.explanation: Implement means take action to put a plan into practice.

cards.statement: A drawback is a disadvantage of an option.
cards.explanation: A drawback is a negative feature or consequence.

cards.statement: A pilot is normally a full national launch of a product.
cards.explanation: A pilot is a limited small-scale test before wider implementation.

cards.statement: A constraint limits what a project can do.
cards.explanation: Constraints can involve time, money, staff, materials or rules.

cards.statement: Innovation and invention are always synonyms in project reports.
cards.explanation: An invention is created for the first time; innovation can also improve an existing idea or process.

cards.statement: Brainstorming happens when people generate ideas, often before judging them.
cards.explanation: Brainstorming is used to produce a range of possible ideas.

cards.statement: Innovation must always mean inventing something that has never existed.
cards.explanation: Innovation can also improve or recombine existing ideas in a valuable way.

activities.explanation: Cada carta repasa una regla del tema; revisa las falladas al terminar el mazo.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 8 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: A trade-off means that every benefit can be obtained without any cost.
cards.explanation: A trade-off involves accepting a cost or disadvantage in exchange for a benefit.

cards.statement: A feasible plan takes available time, money and staff into account.
cards.explanation: Feasible means possible under the actual conditions and resources.

cards.statement: The phrase implement a plan means put it into practice.
cards.explanation: Implement means carry out an agreed plan or system.

cards.statement: Uncertainty means that the result is not fully known, but it does not necessarily mean the result will be negative.
cards.explanation: Uncertainty concerns lack of knowledge; risk specifically highlights a possible negative outcome.

cards.statement: A prototype can reveal design problems before a final product is made.
cards.explanation: Testing an early model helps identify problems cheaply and safely.

cards.statement: A prototype is always the final version of a product.
cards.explanation: A prototype is an early version used for testing and improvement.

cards.statement: A pilot tests a programme on a small scale.
cards.explanation: Pilots reduce the risk of a wider launch by testing an idea first.

cards.statement: To opt for an approach means choose it.
cards.explanation: Opt for is a formal way to say choose.

activities.explanation: Cada carta repasa una regla del tema; revisa las falladas al terminar el mazo.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 5 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: The natural phrase is discuss about the proposal.
cards.explanation: Discuss is transitive: discuss the proposal, without about.

cards.statement: A scalable solution can usually be extended to serve more users or locations.
cards.explanation: Scalability is the capacity to grow without a proportional loss of performance.

cards.statement: Feasible means possible in theory but impossible with current resources.
cards.explanation: Feasible means realistic with the resources, time and conditions available.

cards.statement: To rule out an option means to select it immediately.
cards.explanation: Rule out means eliminate an option from consideration.

cards.statement: A scalable project can grow without losing its effectiveness.
cards.explanation: Scalable describes something that can expand successfully.
